title: Kestrel and the Landfall
premise: Wendell Winterbourne, a desert ranger who has spent twelve years outrunning her past as the salvage fleet's most feared navigator, is hired by old rival Captain Ilsa Vane to race a rival fleet to a wreck that holds proof of Wendell's own buried betrayal. As they cross the drowned flats by tide and starlight, Wendell realizes Vane intends to sell her out to buy peace with the fleet, forcing Wendell to choose between surrendering her found family or finally facing what she did twelve years ago. In the end, Wendell reaches the wreck first, confesses her crime publicly, and gives up her invisibility—keeping her crew not through secrecy but through truth.
about_author: G. M. Brightwater is the pen name of a former tidal surveyor who spent a decade mapping coastal wrecks before turning to fiction. Their work blends hard-won field knowledge with a fascination for people who live just beyond the reach of maps.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Tracking a thief across the salt flats, Wendell catches him only to discover he carries a message from Captain Vane: an offer for the one job Wendell swore off years ago—a run to the Kestrel's wreck. The emotional beat is reluctant curiosity; the thief's knowledge of her past cracks her carefully maintained anonymity.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Shared POV between Wendell and her young deckhand, Sefa. The crew debates taking Vane's contract while the rival salvage fleet mobilizes behind them. Wendell hides the true nature of the cargo from her crew, and the beat is mounting dread as she realizes she's repeating the exact deception that destroyed her old life.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, climaxing in Sefa's discovery of the wreck's manifest naming Wendell as the traitor who sank the original Kestrel. Confronted by Vane mid-storm at the wreck site, Wendell must fight both the sea and the truth. The beat is shattering exposure: her invisibility fails completely, and she nearly loses Sefa to the flood tide.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. After the storm, Wendell stands before the harbor council and confesses everything, forfeiting the salvage rights and her ranger's license rather than let Vane trade her secret. Sefa and the crew choose to stay with her anyway. The beat is quiet redemption: family kept not by secrets, but by honesty—and landfall at last.
